whyChoose.title: What Families in Imperial Beach Should Know

items.title: Strict Filing Deadlines Apply
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Missing these deadlines can close the door on recovery entirely.

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California law prioritizes a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children to bring a wrongful death action, with other dependents or heirs eligible under specific circumstances. An attorney can help clarify who qualifies to pursue a claim.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Medical Bills
items.desc: Because there's no medical treatment to recover for the deceased, California law instead allows families to seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Imperial Beach?
items.answer: Under California law, the general deadline is two years from the date of death. If the claim involves a government agency, such as a city road maintenance issue, the deadline is much shorter, sometimes just months. It's best to start the process early so no options are lost.

items.question: Does Imperial Beach have particular roads connected to more collisions?
items.answer: Public collision records show Palm Avenue, Imperial Beach Boulevard, 13th Street, and 9th Street carry the highest volume of reported crashes in the city, with activity often peaking on Wednesday evenings between 7 and 9 p.m. This pattern reflects traffic volume and reporting data, not a judgment about any specific location.

items.question: What can my family recover in a wrongful death case?
items.answer: California allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Every family's situation is different, and an independent attorney can walk through what applies to yours. LawProactive doesn't provide legal advice directly but can connect you with someone who does.

items.question: Is this the same as a criminal case against the at-fault driver?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensation for the family, while any criminal charges are handled independently by prosecutors. The outcome of one does not determine the outcome of the other.
